An existing, unpaid, informal person, route, or network that repeatedly moves food, goods, care, or information for others and functions as real mobility or distribution infrastructure.

values: Codebook Notes — AV / Food Pantry Co-Design Workshops (DRAFT)
ORDER: The parent codes follow the Literature–Abstract–Data Crosswalk, with subcodes grouped beneath them.
Each abstract concept appears in Column A, with its parent code in Column B.
Column C lists one subcode per row beneath its primary parent. Blue rows are subcodes; parent rows retain their original section colors.
The first code (gray) is the background/framing premise, matching the crosswalk's N/A row.
Last block (yellow) = synthesis concept (Mobility as Social Service), matching the crosswalk's
final row — VALUES leads, with MEANINGS and PRACTICES as supporting evidence.
CARE_INFRA replaces CAPABILITIES in the additional-code block; CONSTRAINTS remains.
CARE_INFRA covers existing recurring unpaid care or distribution networks serving others.
Do not apply CARE_INFRA to isolated skills or resources, one-off errands, or hypothetical networks.
A single excerpt can carry MULTIPLE codes from this list — they are not mutually exclusive.
MISALIGNMENT vs. BREAKDOWN:
MISALIGNMENT = a value-level gap is named (can be calm, reflective).
BREAKDOWN = an in-the-moment interactional reaction (confusion, pushback, redirection).
The same excerpt can carry both.
JUST_ACCESS / JUST_TRUST / JUST_FLEXIBILITY are sub-codes of the broader justice-value moment —
apply as many as fit; don't force a single choice.
Always log workshop ID + speaker role alongside each coded excerpt
(e.g., "Workshop 2 — Pantry Leader, Crystal") so patterns can later be cross-tabbed by role.
Flag any excerpt that doesn't fit cleanly anywhere — these are candidates for new codes
and should be brought to the group, not discarded.
STATUS: DRAFT — pending pilot test with 2 coders on one transcript.
The retained literature-derived subcodes from New Codes Revised are included in Column C.
Their definitions and inclusion criteria are in Column D, exclusions in Column E, and literature sources in Column G.
Example quotes remain blank where the source workbook and revised-code document provide none.
PARENT AND SUBCODE CODING:
Read each blue row as Parent Code (Column B) > Subcode (Column C). A blank Subcode cell identifies a parent definition.
Each subcode appears under one primary parent. Related coding guidance in Column D identifies secondary relationships; apply these only when the passage meets their definitions.
COMMUNITY_BUILT belongs to INPUT_PART_PRESENT; use COGOVERN when community authorship has binding influence. CARE_INFRA applies only to an existing recurring unpaid network.
PERF_VS_AUTH and CONSULT_NO_POWER share INPUT_PART_ABSENT. The former captures an explicit distinction between claimed inclusion and actual power transfer.
CONDITIONALITY belongs to JUST_ACCESS; also use CONSTRAINTS for structural eligibility or deservingness barriers.
FRICTION_MANAGED belongs to BREAKDOWN; also use MISALIGNMENT when a value-level gap is evident.
ACCESS_AS_EFF belongs to EFF_VALUE; also use JUST_ACCESS and add MISALIGNMENT when a value gap is explicit.
EFFICIENCY_SURPLUS belongs to INFRA_FRAME; also use EFF_VALUE and MISALIGNMENT for the efficiency-led exclusion described by the subcode.
